wgc.summary: Q3 total gold demand was broadly steady - 1% lower y/y at 1,369t, while the value of demand rose 22% to US$188bn. Institutional and strategic buyers stepped up: central banks added 321t, up 42% year-on-year, and gold ETFs returned to strong inflows of 211t, lifting holdings to a record 4,256t. By contrast, bar and coin demand fell 19% to 268t given the lack of a clear trend in the gold price, while jewellery demand fell 17% to 313t as gold prices remained high. Technology demand rose 3% to 85t, its highest level since Q4 2021, supported by AI-related manufacturing.
wgc.source: World Gold Council, Gold Demand Trends (public report summary)

points: Mine Production In 2024, global silver mine production rose by 0.9 percent to 819.7 Moz, underpinned by increased output from lead/zinc mines in Australia and the recovery of supply from Mexico, as Newmont’s Peñasquito mine returned to full production.
Lower output from Chile, down 8.8 Moz y/y, partially offset this growth.
In contrast, silver production from gold mines recorded the strongest growth, up 12% y/y to 13.9 Moz, a three-year high.
Recycling Recycling rose 6 percent in 2024, reaching a 12-year high of 193.9 Moz.
In percentage terms, the highest gain came from silverware recycling, which climbed by 11 percent as firmer silver prices and cost-of-living issues encouraged selling in Western markets.
Silver Demand Total silver demand fell by 3 percent to 1.16 billion ounces (Boz) in 2024.
Silverware demand in 2023 fell by 25 percent to 55.2 Moz.
Silver Jewelry and Silverware Silver jewelry fabrication grew by 3 percent to 208.7 Moz in 2024.
Improving exports to key Western countries also lifted fabrication in Thailand by 13 percent.
Silverware demand declined by 2 percent to a three-year low of 54.2 Moz.
Between 1500 and 1800, Bolivia, Peru and Mexico accounted for over 85 percent of world silver production and trade as it bolstered Spanish influence in the New World and elsewhere.
Silver production continued to expand worldwide, growing from 40 to 80 million ounces annually by the 1870s.
Production over the last quarter of the 19th century quadrupled over the average of the first 75 years to a total of nearly 120 million ounces annually.
The twenty years between 1900 and 1920 resulted in a 50 % increase in global production, and brought the total to about 190 million ounces annually.

points: Congo (DRC) and Indonesia. • Chilean production, that currently represents about 21% of world copper mine production, declined by 8% mainly as a result of reduced output at El Teniente, Escondida and Spence mines.

Preliminary data suggests that world apparent refined copper usage increased by 1% in the first nine months of 2026. • World ex-China usage is estimated to have declined by 0.4%, and Chinese apparent demand (excluding changes in bonded/unreported stocks) is estimated to have increased by 2%.

Preliminary world refined copper balance indicates an apparent surplus of 222,000 t in the first nine months of 2026. • In developing its global market balance, ICSG uses an apparent demand calculation for China that does not consider changes in unreported stocks (State Reserve Bureau (SRB), producer, consumer, merchant/trader, bonded).
The world refined copper balance adjusted for estimated changes in Chinese bonded stocks suggested a market surplus of about 185,000 t.

Copper Prices and Stocks: • Based on the average of estimates provided by two independent consultants, China’s bonded stocks are thought to have declined by about 37,000 t in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the year-end 2025 level. • As of the end of October 2026, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 1,068,086 t (highest level since May 2003).

points: Forecast platinum market surplus of 468 koz, widening from previous estimate due primarily to higher-than-expected net disinvestment
Industrial demand revised further upwards (+176 koz) to 2,561 koz, boosted by AI-related applications
Automotive demand remains relatively resilient, despite higher oil prices, at 2,964 koz (-3% year-on-year)
Jewellery demand to decline by 20% to 1,771 koz, reflecting particular weakness in China

Above ground stocks expected to provide just over 3½ months’ global platinum demand cover by the end of 2026, despite the forecast market surplus. This follows a further increase to the 2025 deficit, now estimated at 1.5 Moz, the highest in our series
Expected 747 koz swing to platinum market deficit of 279 koz as total demand growth of 12% outpaces 1% total supply growth
Key driver is a return to investment inflows, mainly due to strong bar and coin demand which is anticipated to increase 55% to 448 koz
Industrial demand growth continues, up 4% (+99 koz) to 2,660 koz, a record for our series, partially offsetting a 5% reduction in automotive demand to 2,813 koz (-151 koz)
Jewellery weakness expected to continue with demand reducing further to 1,710 koz
Above ground stocks to reduce to 1,813 koz - providing just under 3 months’ cover to meet global demand by the end of 2027
